machine value with 0.9 decay factor, interpret the factor

M01.why: same 'points A and B on a circle with center O', 120° central angle, minor arc AB; fixture computes arc length from angle, M01 reverses it and adds a triangle area

within_list_cues.why: both hinge on 'exactly one intersection means the vertex/double root touches'; seeing one solved cues the method for the other (technique, not the numeric answer). Avoid placing in the same module.
both rewrite 4/8 (or nested radicals) as powers of 2 with the same 8 = 2^3 step; mild method overlap only.
both use arc length = r·θ to convert between arc and angle/radius; mild method overlap, no answer cue.

cues_or_overdetermined.issue: format cue: key $10.80 is the only choice with nonzero cents ($9.00, $15.00, $18.00); same flaw that withdrew Q035-09. Make distractors non-round (e.g. $10.00/$12.96) or the key round.

key 1 is the only positive choice and the only one > −2; −2 equals the given x-coordinate and self-eliminates. One sign sketch picks it. Any added choice > −2 would also be correct, so the item needs a sharper condition (e.g. a slope bound) to support several right-of-−2 choices.
key 1 repeats the constant in y > 2x + 1, so 'pick the matching number' guessing works; consider choices like −1, 3, 5, 7 or asking for the greatest k.
mild: 75 is the only choice not a multiple of 20 (60, 80, 160).

mild: key is the intersection choice (shares (t − 3) with one choice and 44.1 with another); 'displays the maximum as a constant' also eliminates the factored form at sight. Also mirrors the well-known official SAT 'which equivalent form displays ... as a constant or coefficient' format.

stem wording gives the answer: A is described as 'very close to the line', B as 'widely scattered', and the key repeats 'lie closer to its line'. Describe the plots neutrally (or show them) so the slope trap actually bites.
mild: the key is the only choice that is both random-selection and random-assignment and the longest; inherent to the format, but balance lengths.

official_mirrors: K09 mirrors the released official SAT 'equivalent form that displays [max/min/intercepts] as a constant or coefficient' item format. J08 (round trip at two speeds), J13 (give-$20 puzzle) and M04 (shared-angle similar triangles AD·AC = AB²) are textbook classics but not close to a specific released SAT item.
